analyst_view.overall: Everton (9th) host Liverpool (4th) in the Merseyside derby at Sunday lunchtime. Everton lost 4-0 at Brentford on Monday, where captain James Tarkowski was sent off; he starts a three-match ban, Michael Keane is the likely replacement and Jack Grealish is back in David Moyes' squad, which otherwise came through fit. Andoni Iraola's Liverpool won 3-0 at Club Brugge on Wednesday night (Isak twice, Wirtz), but Victor Munoz left that game on a stretcher with a knee knock and is a major doubt, and they have under four days before kick-off. Gakpo (out) and Gravenberch (likely out) are now in the numbers, as are Tarkowski's ban, the derby's extra cards (+39%) and referee Michael Oliver's average record, so I only size Munoz and the short turnaround.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals (Everton 1.1, Liverpool 1.4), and they now include Tarkowski's ban and Gakpo and Gravenberch being out, so my earlier cut for Gakpo is gone. What is still new is Munoz's knee knock from Bruges and a Sunday 12:00 kick-off less than four days after a Wednesday night away game; Liverpool looked sharp in Belgium, so I trim only a little, to about 2.45.

corners.text: The numbers expect 10.4 corners, with Liverpool's high corner count lately (+9%) already counted. Losing Munoz would take away a wide runner, but Ngumoha and the full-backs still give Liverpool width, and Everton without Tarkowski may defend deeper; that points both ways, so I stay at about 10.4.

cards.text: The numbers expect 4.9 cards, already including the derby boost (about +39%) and Michael Oliver's average record (4.0 a game). Tarkowski's ban removes Everton's most aggressive defender rather than adding anything, so I see nothing new and stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers expect 29.7 shots, 17.6 from Liverpool after a +16% boost from their heavy shooting lately. The Wednesday night trip to Bruges, the early Sunday kick-off and Munoz's doubt are not in the numbers, so I take about 3% off, to about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers expect 9.1 shots on target (Everton 4.2, Liverpool 4.9), with both sides' form counted. Isak and Wirtz are in form, so the only new factors are Liverpool's short turnaround and Munoz's knock; I make a small 2% cut, to about 8.9.
